# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

WHEN June drew to a close, the term reached its end, as did the reign of Miss Thorne at the school in Brierley. That evening, Nell and Isolde experienced a truly solemn mood as they made their way home. The presence of wet handkerchiefs and red eyes offered clear proof that the parting remarks of Miss Thorne had been just as moving as those delivered by Mr. Pidgeon during a comparable situation three years earlier. From the base of the spruce-covered hill, Isolde cast a glance behind her toward the schoolhouse and let out a heavy sigh.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0000 }

“It truly appears as though all things have come to a close, wouldn’t you say?” she asked mournfully.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0001 }

“It isn't right for you to be even half as upset as me,” Nell remarked, searching fruitlessly to find any part of her handkerchief that was dry. “You will return when next winter comes, whereas I imagine I am gone from our beloved former school for good—assuming I am fortunate, of course.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0002 }

“It will be entirely different. Miss Thorne will not be present, and you, Odette, and likely Opal will be missing as well. My seat will have to be completely solitary, because I could not tolerate anyone else sharing a desk with me once you are gone. Oh, our times together were wonderful, were they not, Nell? Knowing they are completely finished is terrible.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0003 }

A pair of large tears trickled beside Isolde’s nose.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0004 }

“I would be able to if you stopped weeping,” Nell pleaded. “No sooner do I store my handkerchief than I spot your eyes welling with tears, which triggers me once more. To quote Mrs. Sowerby, ‘If you can’t be cheerful, be as cheerful as you can.’ When all is said and done, I expect I will return the following year. I am certain I will fail on this occasion. Such instances are becoming frighteningly common.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0005 }

“Indeed, your performance on the tests administered by Miss Thorne was exceptional.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0006 }

“Yes, however I was not made nervous by those exams. You are unable to conceive the terrible cold fluttery sensation that encompasses my heart when I contemplate the actual event. Furthermore, my assigned number is thirteen, which Flossie Tulk claims brings terrible luck. Being unsuperstitious, I realize that it is incapable of altering the outcome. Nevertheless, I prefer that it were not thirteen.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0007 }

“I really wish I was accompanying you inside,” Isolde said. “Wouldn’t we enjoy a thoroughly splendid time? Still, I imagine you will need to study hard during the evenings.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0008 }

“No; Miss Thorne has required a promise from us to refrain entirely from opening a book. According to her, it would merely exhaust and muddle us, so we ought to take walks, avoid thinking about the exams whatsoever, and turn in early. Although it is sound counsel, I anticipate difficulty in adhering to it; sound counsel usually is, in my opinion. It was Sukey Pullen who informed me that throughout her Entrance week she remained awake for half the night each evening to cram frantically; consequently, I had resolved to stay awake for a duration no shorter than hers. Your Aunt Lavinia was exceedingly gracious to invite me to reside at Beechwood during my time in town.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0009 }

“While you are there, you will send me letters, will you not?”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0010 }

“I’ll send a letter Tuesday evening to let you know how my initial day turns out,” Nell promised.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0011 }

“On Wednesday, I will be lingering around the post office,” promised Isolde.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0012 }

When the next Monday arrived, Nell traveled to town, and on Wednesday, following their agreement, Isolde waited around the post office until she received her letter.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0013 }

“Dearest Isolde” [wrote Nell],
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0014 }

“Tuesday night has arrived and the Beechwood library is where I am writing this. My room was dreadfully lonely last night while I was all by myself, making me wish deeply for your presence. Having given my word to Miss Thorne that I wouldn’t, I couldn't ‘cram,’ though refraining from unclosing my history book proved just as difficult as avoiding a storybook before finishing my lessons used to be.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0015 }

“Miss Thorne fetched me earlier today, and our journey to the Academy included stopping to pick up Odette, Opal, and Flossie. Opal requested that I touch her hands, which felt like ice. Flossie remarked that I appeared to have not slept at all, adding that she doubted my strength to endure the grueling nature of the teacher’s course even in the event of my passing. Even now, certain moments arise when I doubt I have made much progress toward growing fond of Flossie Tulk!
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0016 }

“Upon our arrival at the Academy, dozens of pupils gathered there had come from every part of the Island. Sitting on the steps, Elias Purdy was the very first individual we encountered, and he was mumbling to himself. When Odette inquired what in the world he was up to, he replied that he was reciting the multiplication table repeatedly to calm his anxiety and begged for goodness’ sake not to break his concentration, since pausing even briefly made him terrified and erased all the knowledge he had ever acquired, whereas the multiplication table anchored every piece of information securely where it belonged!
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0017 }

“When our rooms were assigned to us Miss Thorne was forced to depart from us. Odette and I took seats beside one another and Odette possessed such composure that it made me envious of her. Good, steady, sensible Odette had no requirement for the multiplication table! I questioned whether my appearance matched my feelings and whether my heart could be heard thumping by them all the way across the room. After that a man entered and started handing out the English examination sheets. My hands turned cold right then and my head literally spun as I lifted it. Merely one terrible moment—Isolde, my feelings were precisely the same as four years back when my request to stay at Grey Shutters was put to Thirza—and after that all became clear within my mind and my heart commenced beating once more—I neglected to mention that its beating had ceased entirely!—because I was aware that I could manage something with that paper at least.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0018 }

“We returned home for dinner at noon, after which we went back for history in the afternoon. That history exam was quite difficult, and my dates became terribly confused. Even so, I believe my performance today was fairly good. However, oh, Isolde, the geometry exam takes place tomorrow, and contemplating it requires all the resolve I have to refrain from opening my Euclid. If I believed it would be of any assistance, I would recite the multiplication table continuously until tomorrow morning.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0019 }

“This evening I went down for a visit with the other girls. As I was going, I encountered Elias Purdy walking about in a distracted manner. He told me he knew he had failed his history exam and was destined to disappoint his parents, so he intended to leave on the morning train; moreover, he remarked that working as a carpenter would be simpler than becoming a minister. I comforted him and convinced him to remain until the conclusion, pointing out that leaving early would be unkind to Miss Thorne. There are times when I have desired to be a boy, yet whenever I observe Elias Purdy, I feel grateful to be a girl and relieved that I am not his sister.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0020 }

“Opal was hysterical as I arrived at their boarding-house, having only recently realized the terrible error she committed on her English exam. After she calmed down, we traveled uptown to eat ice cream. We longed for you to be there alongside us.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0021 }

“Oh, Isolde, I wish the test in geometry was already finished! Still, as Mrs. Sowerby is accustomed to saying, the sun is going to keep coming up and going down regardless of my failing geometry. Though that is accurate, it does not bring much solace. My preference, I believe, would be for it to stop if I were to fail!
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0022 }

“Yours devotedly,
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0023 }

“Nell”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0024 }

When the geometry test alongside the remaining exams concluded at the expected hour, Nell returned to her house that Friday night, feeling fairly exhausted yet carrying a subdued sense of victory. Isolde happened to be visiting Grey Shutters at the moment of her arrival, and their greeting was as dramatic as though an eternity had passed since they last saw each other.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0025 }

“You dear old thing, seeing you return is absolutely wonderful. Your departure for town feels like an eternity ago, and oh, Nell, how did things go for you?”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0026 }

“I believe I did fairly well, except for geometry. Whether I passed that subject is uncertain to me, and I possess a strange, uneasy feeling that I failed. Ah, returning here brings such joy! Grey Shutters remains the most cherished, exquisite place on earth.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0027 }

“In what manner did the rest perform?”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0028 }

“ Although the girls claim to be certain of their failure, my impression is that they performed quite admirably. According to Flossie, the geometry problem was simple enough for a ten-year-old child! Elias Purdy continues to believe he flopped in history, while Wilfred claims to have flunked algebra. Nevertheless, we remain completely in the dark and will continue to be until the pass list is published. Two weeks will pass before that happens. Imagine existing for a full fortnight in such anxiety! If only I could fall asleep and not awaken until the waiting is finished.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0029 }

Because Isolde recognized that inquiring about the outcome for Hugh Carrow would serve no purpose, she simply remarked:
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0030 }

“Oh, you’ll get through without a problem. Do not fret.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0031 }

“I’d rather not pass at all than not come out pretty well up on the list,” Nell declared impetuously, expressing the idea—which Isolde fully understood—that any victory would feel flawed and resentful unless she placed higher than Hugh Carrow.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0032 }

To achieve this goal, Nell had pushed herself to the utmost throughout the tests. Hugh had done the same. On twelve occasions they had encountered one another while walking, offering no indication of knowing each other, and on each occasion Nell had raised her chin slightly more, desired with greater intensity that she had befriended Hugh upon his request, and resolved with firmer intent to beat him in the test. She was aware that the entire lower school at Brierley debated who would take top place; she was aware as well that Ned Duckett and Jimmy Glover possessed a wager regarding the outcome and that Flossie Tulk had declared Hugh was certain to come first beyond any doubt; and she believed that missing the top spot would cause her unacceptable shame.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0033 }

Yet a different and finer reason urged her to succeed. On account of Obed and Thirza—Obed above all—she desired to “pass high.” Obed had stated to her his belief that she “would beat the whole Island.” Even in the most fantastical dreams, Nell believed, hoping for that was absurd. Nevertheless, she did earnestly wish to rank in the top ten at minimum, enabling her to watch Obed’s warm brown eyes shine with satisfaction at her accomplishment. For all her strenuous efforts and quiet labor over dry equations and conjugations, that, she thought, would truly be a delightful recompense.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0034 }

When the two weeks concluded, Nell began "haunting" the post office as well, alongside the agitated Odette, Opal, and Flossie, unsealing the Port Marlow newspapers with trembling fingers and chilled, nauseating sensations that rivaled any felt throughout the Entrance week. Wilfred and Hugh were equally willing to engage in this behavior, yet Elias Purdy remained firmly absent.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0035 }

“I lack the courage to head over and examine a result sheet deliberately,” he confessed to Nell. “My plan is simply to hold off until a person arrives and abruptly informs me if I passed or failed.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0036 }

As three weeks passed with no pass list in sight, Nell started to think she truly was unable to bear the tension for much longer. She lost her appetite, and her enthusiasm for Brierley events waned. Mrs. Sowerby inquired about what other outcome one might anticipate when a Tory superintendent of education led affairs, while Obed, observing Nell’s pale face, her lack of interest, and the slow pace at which she returned from the post office each afternoon, commenced earnest consideration of whether he ought to cast a Grit vote in the upcoming election.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0037 }

However, the information arrived on a certain evening. Forgetful for the moment of world anxieties and examination troubles, Nell sat by her unclosed window and absorbed the charm of the summer twilight, which breathed sweet scents from the flowerbeds beneath and sounded whispering and rustling with the movement of poplar trees. The eastern heavens over the fir trees were tinted a delicate rose by the reflected light of the setting sun, and Nell was musing absently whether the spirit of color possessed such an appearance, when she noticed Isolde racing downward through the firs, across the log bridge, and up the incline, clutching a waving newspaper in her hand.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0038 }

Nell leapt up, immediately recognizing the contents of that document. The results of the examination were published! A feeling of dizziness overcame her head, and her heart pounded to the point of pain. She found herself incapable of taking a single step. To her, it felt like an hour passed prior to Isolde racing down the corridor and charging into the chamber without bothering to knock, driven by her immense state of agitation.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0039 }

“Nell, you passed,” she exclaimed, “passed at the absolute top—you as well as Hugh—the two of you tied—however your name comes first. Oh, my heart is brimming with pride!”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0040 }

Isolde cast the document upon the table and threw herself onto the bed belonging to Nell, completely winded and unable to say another word. Nell set fire to the lamp's wick, knocking over the match container and expending six matches prior to her trembling fingers completing the action. Following that, she grabbed the document. Indeed, she had succeeded—her name appeared at the absolute head of a roster containing two hundred! Existing for that single instant was genuinely worthwhile.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0041 }

“Nell, your performance was simply wonderful,” Isolde gasped out, regaining enough breath to sit upright and address her, since Nell, with glowing eyes and an enchanted expression, had remained completely silent. “Dad brought the newspaper from Alder River barely ten minutes back—it arrived via the afternoon train, as you are aware, and the post won't deliver it here until tomorrow—so the moment I spotted the list of successful candidates, I tore over here like a madwoman. All of you have succeeded, every single one, even Elias Purdy, though he has a condition in history. Odette and Opal scored fairly well—they are positioned in the middle—and Wilfred did too. Flossie barely made it with a mere three-point margin, yet you can bet she will act just as haughty as if she had come out on top. Won't Miss Thorne be thrilled? Oh, Nell, how does it feel to behold your own name right at the top of a pass list like that? Were I in your place, I am certain I would lose my mind from happiness. I feel almost wild with excitement myself, yet you remain as serene and chilled as a spring night.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0042 }

“My mind is simply overwhelmed,” Nell stated. “There are a hundred things I wish to express, yet the phrasing eludes me. Such a thing was beyond my imagination—actually, no, I imagined it a single time! A single time I permitted myself to ponder, ‘What if the top position ends up being mine?’ with much trepidation, as you can imagine, because assuming I might top the Island felt exceedingly arrogant and conceited. Give me just a moment, Isolde. I need to dash out to the field immediately so I can inform Obed. After that, we will proceed up the road to share the fortunate report with everyone else.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0043 }

They rushed down to the hayfield beneath the barn, where Obed was making haycocks, and, fortunately, Mrs. Sowerby was conversing with Thirza by the lane fence.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0044 }

“Oh, Obed,” Nell cried out, “I got through, and my mark is at the top—or nearly at the top! Vanity isn't my motive, but gratitude is.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0045 }

“Well now, I always said it,” Obed remarked, looking at the pass list with delight. “I knew you could beat them all easy.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0046 }

“I must say, Nell, you have performed quite well,” Thirza remarked, attempting to conceal her deep pride in Nell from Mrs. Agatha’s discerning gaze. Nevertheless, that kind-hearted woman declared with warmth:
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0047 }

“I simply reckon she has succeeded, and I would certainly not hold back from stating as much. You bring honor to your companions, Nell, indeed you do, and every one of us is proud of you.”
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0048 }

Later that evening Nell, who concluded the enchanting night by having a grave short conversation with Mrs. Wace in the manse, was kneeling sweetly near her open window amid a grand radiance of moonlight and uttered a prayer of thanks and longing that originated directly from her heart. Within it was appreciation for days gone by along with a respectful plea for what lay ahead; and as she lay sleeping upon her white pillow her dreams proved to be just as lovely and brilliant and wonderful as a young girl could wish for.
{: #nw-v01-c32-p0049 }
